the motifs of the Res subunit, which are conserved among all the type III restriction/modification enzymes, are involved in the ATP-dependent reactions of the EcoPI enzyme.
mutations in motifs I and/or II of EcoPI restriction enzyme affect ATP hydrolysis, and that mutations in motif I, but not motif II, affect DNA cleavage.
the motifs I and II of EcoPI restriction enzyme are involved in ATP-dependent reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the EcoPI type III restriction/modification system.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of DNA restriction by type III enzymes, which is a subject of considerable interest in the field of molecular biology.
the molecular mechanisms of the EcoPI type III DNA restriction enzyme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
motifs II and I are involved in the ATPase activity of EcoPI and motif I is involved in the coupling of DNA cleavage to ATP hydrolytic reaction.
motifs I and II are required for the ATP-dependent translocations in the EcoPI restriction enzymes.
motif I is involved in the coupling of ATPase and cleavage reactions and motif II is involved in the translocation of EcoPI restriction enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ATPase activity of the Res subunit is required for restriction activity, and the DNA helicase-like activity of the Res is not.
the ATP-dependent DNA cleavage by a type III restriction-modificatin enzyme is not dependent on DNA unwinding.
the ATPase activity of the Res subunit is essential for DNA cleavage by the type III restriction enzyme EcoPI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Res subunit has a dual function: it binds ATP and is involved in ATP hydrolysis, and it also plays an important structural role in DNA cleavage.
the ATP-dependent reaction of the type III enzymes is a complex process involving at least two different ATPase reaction centres.
type III restriction enzymes have a unique mode of DNA recognition and restriction that is not shared by any other restriction system.
